findings.F1: The check fails on Calmar alone (0.60 against 0.75). The chained book's deepest fall is −33.0 % against a yearly return of +19.9 %, and that fall runs 217 days from w1 to w3, while holding the coins lost 65.9 % over the same stretch. Book returns were −6.6 %, −13.9 % and −8.0 % in w1, w2 and w3, and its deepest falls inside one window are −23.8 % (w3), −21.9 % (w14) and −20.6 % (w18), all windows where holding lost (−10 %, −49 %, −22 %).
findings.F2: The dips that rebound are the ones whose week is still rising. Across 1,887 recomputed cases, the unusual 72-hour return rises steadily with the coin's 7-day return:
findings.F3: The dip's own depth does not grade the rebound; the 30-day and 7-day trends do.
findings.F4: Losses cluster in dips taken far below the coin's 30-day high.
findings.F5: Dips in a quiet market pay less than dips in a volatile one.
findings.F6: Size is not the problem. The total move is +0.96 % per case, 5.0 times the 0.19 % cost of a trade, and the unusual move is 2.9 times that cost. The failure comes from deep falls in collapsing markets, not from costs.

ideas.idea: When a coin's 24-hour return, read at an hourly close, falls by several times its 30-day average absolute daily return while its 30-day return is positive, the coin rises over the next 3 days more than its normal drift, only while its 7-day return is positive, and the higher its 7-day return, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: Buy a sharp one-day drop in a month-long rise only when the past week is still up, sized up the stronger that week, and refuse dips whose week has already turned down, which is where the deep losses sit.
ideas.name: dip in rising week rebounds

ideas.idea: When a coin's 24-hour return, read at an hourly close, falls by several times its 30-day average absolute daily return while its 30-day return is positive, the coin rises over the next 3 days more than its normal drift, and the closer the coin's close is to its 30-day high, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A sharp drop taken near the month's high is a reason to buy for a few days, while one taken far below the high is a reason to hold back, because those dips carry most of the deep losses.
ideas.name: dip near monthly high rebounds

ideas.idea: When a coin's 24-hour return falls by several times its 30-day average absolute daily return while its 30-day return is positive, the coin rises over the next 3 days more than its normal drift, and the higher its 7-day volatility relative to its 60-day volatility, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: Size dip-buys in a rising month up when the past week has been unusually volatile, and down when the market has been quiet, where the dips do not rebound.
ideas.name: volatile dip rebounds more
